A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Learn2Synth and retain matching core equations and experiments. The text, figures, tables, and supplementary sections are readable and support comparison throughout.

before.justification: v1 reports original noise-parameter inference experiments and segmentation results on synthetic images, ABIDE, OASIS3, and Buckner40.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds FLASH generalization experiments, validation-selection comparisons, and an unpaired segmentation experiment.

M1.justification: The main algorithm and Equations (1)–(11) remain unchanged, but v2 Supplement Section 9 introduces a substantial unpaired GAN extension. It adds generator/discriminator training and an adversarial hypergradient objective using independent segmentation maps and real scans, removing the paired-real-label requirement for this variant.

E1.justification: v2 adds the eight-subject FreeSurfer maintenance dataset, evaluating FLASH scans at 3, 5, 20, and 30 degrees after MPRAGE training. This introduces explicitly unseen imaging contrasts beyond v1's coverage. The Buckner40/Buckner39 descriptions represent retained brain-imaging coverage; the name and sample-count revision alone is not a new domain.

E2.justification: The ABIDE/OASIS3 comparison adds evaluated Mixed SynthSeg and Finetuned SynthSeg baselines in v2 Table 5. The reworked Buckner comparison includes supervised UNet, explicitly absent from that comparison in v1, and no longer includes SAMSEG. These changes substantially expand comparisons against alternative uses of real training data.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates Buckner using ABIDE/OASIS3 training samples. v2 introduces training with 1, 5, or 29 labeled Buckner scans, five validation scans, and corresponding held-out test sets, while retaining ABIDE/OASIS3 label maps for synthesis. It also compares validation-selected and final checkpoints. The reported Buckner dataset size changes from 40 to 39.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial robustness and sensitivity analyses: transfer across FLASH contrasts, performance under three labeled-training budgets, and validation-selected versus final checkpoints (Tables 6–7 and Figure 4). Existing synthetic noise/INU analyses largely remain, although v1's table of nonparametric inferred-noise values is omitted.

E5.justification: v1 reports point estimates, whereas v2 adds plus/minus values in Tables 6–7 and the unpaired experiment, along with boxplots in Figure 4. Their statistical meaning is not defined, and neither version specifies repeated-run or seed counts. This establishes additional uncertainty reporting, not additional experimental repetitions or significance testing.

E6.justification: v2 adds mixed/fine-tuned baseline results, extensive MPRAGE/FLASH results, checkpoint comparisons, and an unpaired Dice score of 0.874 ± 0.0104. Naive SynthSeg's ABIDE/OASIS3 entries change from 0.866/0.829 to 0.869/0.831. Retained synthetic accuracy tables match exactly. v1's nonparametric noise estimates and original Buckner variant results are omitted or replaced; the new Buckner scores use different training conditions.

T1.justification: The hypergradient derivation and mathematical definitions of the parametric and nonparametric augmentation models in Equations (1)–(11) are retained. The GAN extension is described procedurally and schematically, without a new formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The central contribution of learning synthesis through real-data hypergradients while training the segmenter on synthetic data remains. v2's contribution list and conclusion explicitly claim superior unseen-contrast generalization relative to supervised training, and the conclusion also names SynthSeg. v1 makes broader generalization claims but leaves further exploration to future work.

C2.justification: v2 recommends a known low-dimensional parametric model over a nonparametric alternative and interprets the checkpoint analysis as permitting five labeled examples without five additional validation examples. It also develops the interpretation of unseen-contrast transfer. The main mechanism explanation and stated limitations concerning paired target labels and 2D experiments remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies 434 source images for the synthetic study, 60/20/20 splits for retained experiments, coronal slicing, random initialization, class identities, and the four-level UNet architecture. These are substantial documentation additions, without establishing changes to previously undisclosed settings. Conversely, v1's batch size of 64 is omitted. Adam, the learning rate, and code availability are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations covering DatasetGAN, other generative segmentation and one-shot synthesis work, the FLASH dataset, Adam, and V-Net. It removes DAGAN and Learning to Compose citations. The central positioning relative to domain randomization, distribution-matching synthesis, and hypergradient optimization remains.

P1.justification: v2 substantially condenses and rewrites related work and experimental explanations, incorporates the former Learning strategy section into Method, consolidates synthetic subsections, and reorganizes real-data experiments around two explicit questions. The title gains a brain-segmentation qualifier, author information changes, and acknowledgements are added.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the two training-pass diagrams with a redesigned comparison schematic, merges v1 Tables 4 and 6, and extensively reformats and relocates tables. It adds the FLASH results visualization and GAN diagram, reduces the earlier qualitative segmentation panel, and removes the real-world synthesis illustration. These changes go well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: The new MPRAGE-to-FLASH study directly strengthens v1's weakly tested generalization claim, while mixed-training and fine-tuning comparisons address important alternative uses of real data. Checkpoint analysis and fuller protocol documentation further improve assessability. Undefined uncertainty terms, the omitted batch size, and failures with one training scan limit the broader claims, but the new controlled evidence provides a substantial net improvement.
